rawFindings.title: Incorrect population model fallback allowing undefined modelName
rawFindings.explanation: The original code allowed falling back to `model.modelName` if neither `options.model` nor `schema.options.ref` was set for the populate model name. This could cause population to proceed with an incorrect or undefined model name. The change fixes this by restricting the modelName to only `options.model` or `schema.options.ref`, and errors out otherwise, preventing silent failure or invalid behavior.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep the changed code that removes fallback to `model.modelName` and instead throws an error if `modelName` cannot be determined.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Population with options lacking `model` and schema lacking `ref` now causes an error instead of using an incorrect or undefined model name leading to population errors.

rawFindings.title: Test cases expect error on missing populate model name
rawFindings.explanation: The test was changed to expect an error when populating with missing model name rather than no error. This aligns with the fix above ensuring invalid configurations now result in an error.
rawFindings.suggestion: Maintain the changed test assertion `assert.ok(err)` to verify that an error is returned for invalid population model specifications.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Tests will fail if no error is returned on invalid population invocation lacking model name.

rawFindings.title: Test cases expect error on missing populate model name
rawFindings.explanation: Also changed test assertion to expect error on invalid populate model name situation, consistent with defect fix.
rawFindings.suggestion: Maintain the changed test with `assert.ok(err)` to validate error is thrown on missing model in populate call.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Tests fail if no error is thrown on populate missing a model name due to invalid input.
